**Compute Occupied Voxels:** A voxel is strictly occupied if all 8 of its corner neighbors are occupied.
For a voxel at $(x,y,z)$, this requires checking indices $(x+i, y+j, z+k)$ for $i,j,k \in \{0, 1\}$.
**Compute Unoccupied Voxels:** A voxel is strictly unoccupied if all 8 of its corner neighbors are empty.
This is the negation of the logical OR of the 8 neighbors.
**Determine Boundary Voxels:** A voxel is on the boundary if it is neither strictly occupied nor strictly unoccupied.
This is calculated as the logical AND of the negations of the occupied and unoccupied masks.
**Expand Boundary (Optional):** If `boundarySize` > 1, the initial boundary mask is dilated.
The neighborhood size is adjusted to be odd if even.
Bounds are clamped to the grid dimensions.
Let $O[x,y,z]$ be the occupancy value at $(x,y,z)$.
